name: Judeo-Kashani
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 10 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Borjian, Habib. 2012. Judeo-Kashani: A Central Iranian Plateau Dialect. Journal of the American Oriental Society 132(1): 1-21. (JSTOR stable 10.7817/jameroriesoci.132.1.0001; open copy: archive.org item JudeoKashaniACentralIranianPlateauDialect)
catalog_locator: Article p. 3, Phonology §1.7 (of the saved JSTOR PDF.); supporting lines p. 2 editorial note on stress marks, p. 3 §1.6 and §2.1(2)
catalog_quote: §1.7. Stress is only documented by Žukovskij, but it is perhaps a mixture of morphological and emphatic types of stress. As in other CPDs the stress appears to be word final in nouns and word initial in verbs. [p. 3] ... Stress marks are reproduced when they are not predictably word final. Other necessary phonological adjustments are ignored in the reproduced Texts, but are made ... when words and phrases are quoted in the Grammar and Glossary. These include ignoring the vowel length (see §1.2.1) and the stress marks, which sometimes lack distinction between morphological and syntactical accentuation [p. 2] ... §1.6. A stem following a stressed prefix may lose its initial consonant: da-ᵍir-om (‘that I seize’) ~ m-e-gireᵗ (‘I used to seize’); be-ᵛin-om (‘that I see’) ~ vin-e (‘you see’). [p. 3] ... (2) Indefinite markers are itå (‘one’) and the unstressed suffix -i, as in itå šaw (‘a night’), rúji (‘a day’). [p. 3 §2.1]
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: §1.7. Stress is only documented by Žukovskij, but it is perhaps a mixture of morphological and emphatic types of stress. As in other CPDs the stress appears to be word final in nouns and word initial in verbs.
new_statements.citation: Borjian, Habib. 2012. Judeo-Kashani: A Central Iranian Plateau Dialect. Journal of the American Oriental Society 132(1): 1-21. JSTOR stable URL 10.7817/jameroriesoci.132.1.0001
new_statements.locator: p. 3, Phonology §1.7 (PDF page 4 of the archive.org scan)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (22 pp., JSTOR-cover + article pp. 1-21; text present, extracted text works; same text in lines 179-181). Passage found exactly at the stated locator, article p. 3 = PDF page 4, under the 'phonology' heading, §1.7, verbatim apart from the line-break hyphenation 'morphologi-/cal': "§1.7. Stress is only documented by Žukovskij, but it is perhaps a mixture of morphological and emphatic types of stress. As in other CPDs the stress appears to be word final in nouns and word initial in verbs." Surrounding section read: §1.6 (p. 3) 'A stem following a stressed prefix may lose its initial consonant: da-gir-om.. be-vin-om' supports the verb-initial (prefix-stressed) half; p. 2 editorial note 'S…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Nouns carry word stress on the final syllable; verbs carry it on the initial syllable (i.e., on the verbal prefix/preverb, cf. §1.6 'A stem following a stressed prefix may lose its initial consonant'). The author hedges: the only stress marks are Žukovskij's 19th-century transcriptions, which may mix morphological and emphatic stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Verbs are stressed word-initially rather than finally; the indefinite suffix -i is unstressed (§2.1: 'the unstressed suffix -i, as in itå šaw, rúji'); Žukovskij's marks 'sometimes lack distinction between morphological and syntactical accentuation' (p. 2).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, based on stress marks in Žukovskij's transcribed texts (translated Persian sentences and tales, Materialy vol. 2: 390-94), not on live elicitation; the dialect is extinct in Kashan.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog soii1239 "Soic/Soi" is a cover languoid: hh.bib maps Judeo-Kashani, Jowshaqani, Meyma'i, Keša'i, Abuzeydabadi and the Barzoki Raji dialect all to Soi [soj]; Ethnologue/Wikipedia treat Judeo-Kashani as a dialect of Soi. The quoted statement describes Judeo-Kashani (the extinct urban Jewish dialect of Kashan, documented from Žukovskij's 1880s texts), not the Sō/Soh village dialect proper (Andreas 1939, Mann-Hadank 1926). No separate glottocode exists for Judeo-Kashani. Borjian frames the pattern as shared by Central Plateau dialects generally ("As in other CPDs").
